items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: Pee Wee has never played anything he didn't intend to play

ctx.x: half the time because she's reading that could be sure what was happening or for that matter might not even distinguish from it I think there are too few examples for us to dwell on that subject in fact I'm frightened by it because I know how imperfect my ear is and how exact an instrument could show those differences

Pee Wee in ensemble work is a wonderful example of that when Pee Wee will play a chorus that has many atonalities let's say in it then you listen to him in the ensemble it'll be clean as a whistle and right on the button and those high notes are beautiful he'd never do it then he'd only do it when he's expressing himself on some in a way exactly the way he wanted to Pee Wee has never played anything he didn't intend to play

I'm sure that we've begun to get into a marsh of questions here beyond the scope of common understanding and when you talk about the musician being a critic this is only where the musician can tread with safety is in these matters of the tempered scale and understanding of these slight shadings
